summary: The scanner now never opens the Windows container layer store (%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers). `ContainerLayerStore.Resolve` finds it once per scan: a string check first, then a final-path check by handle on the root and the store's anchor. A scan above the store records it as one not-scanned folder (`SkippedStores`, `EntryFlags.NotScanned`, kept out of `Unreadable`), and a backstop in `DirectoryReader.Read` refuses and counts any listing under it. A root at or inside the store comes back as a new `Refused` outcome, and the window and the `--report` output say why. All of this is behind one precaution switch that is on by default. The repro test now passes, with WCsc and the System handle count unchanged on this fresh boot. Tests built: 32 new temp-tree tests, 14 cases for the protocol judge, window cases X-001 to X-004, and 13 harness plants (all AS-RECORDED). The person-run pool protocol (`PoolWatch.ps1`, the ScanArm rig, hook triggers) ran end to end in smoke mode. The design record holds the measured tag owners, the environment, and the tolerance row written before any run. DONE (c) itself still needs the person's Start > Restart protocol.

obligations.how: M1: the design record says the Files tree holds real bytes (the pristine copies of the dynamic base image), so the whole-store exclusion drops real bytes. The open question is reworded to cover Layers\<id>\Files as well. The row text reads 'size not counted: Windows container layers'. The store's byte upper bound is taken once by -Prepare on the pre-Restart boot with robocopy /L /E /XJ /BYTES (Y4 replaces the dir positive control). It is never added to any total.

M2: -Protocol runs R0, then I0, then arm L (the app's listing-only walk, store excluded) first, then S and P, then the exe runs. L's cold cost is judged against T from L/before. A second session runs only if L is over T (Q-185).

M3: the pressure step (PoolWatch -PressureChild) runs after the cancelled arms. It commits memory down to 4,608 MB available (X2/N3 put the floor above the 4,096 MB guard instead of 90%) and holds it. -Report counts tags that fall as cache and routes to C only from post-pressure figures. The 32 MiB warm-repeat cap came from an earlier row; the current row judges each run and the cumulative total against T.

M4: -Prepare publishes afd021d through git archive, without touching the work tree. -Protocol runs U1 and U2 (unfixed, full) and U3 (unfixed, cancelled past the store) AFTER the closing control, as Y1's later decision moved them.

M5: ScanResult.SkippedStores is its own list and never enters Unreadable. The report carries core.skippedStores apart from core.unreadable. Tested by AnUnreadableFolderAndTheStoreAreRecordedApart and WindowCases X-004 (461 unreadable, 1 skipped).

M6: DirectoryReader's backstop counter is published as opensUnderExcludedStore and must be 0. Drift is estimated per gap with bursts over 3x the median left out. The handle rise must be at most the WCsc rise (plus 48 for churn). N2 later narrowed 'ambient' to rises inside the idle envelope.

m1: Resolve's handle step uses GetFinalPathNameByHandleW on the root and the anchor, then rebases the store into the root's spelling. Tested by ARootThroughASubstDriveAboveTheStoreStopsAtIt, ARootThroughAJunctionAboveTheStoreStopsAtIt, ARootSpelledWithTheVolumeGuidStopsAtTheStore and ARootSpelledWithShortNamesStopsAtTheStore (the 8.3 root turns out to be expanded by GetFullPath).

m2: popped paths are compared for equality, as listed and without case, never through GetFullPath. SiblingsNamedLayersDotAndLayersSpaceAreCounted creates 'Layers.' and 'Layers ' through \\?\ and counts both.

m4: DirectoryReader.Read is the only caller of OpenDirectory, and a settled rule plus plant S22 enforce that. Read refuses any path at or under the excluded store without opening it and counts it. The pop-time check stays as the fast path. Tested by TheReaderRefusesAndCountsAFolderUnderTheStoreWithNoOpen.

m5, as accepted: X-002 covers ...\Containers (skippedStores 1, opensUnderExcludedStore 0, unreadable not counting it). X-004 adds the report field with unreadable folders. read-window -Outcome reads the fields. The AssemblyName rename was declined by the decision. The repro skips with a reason when there is no layer.

m6: cancels are set from progress (FSA_HOOK_PAST=store or C:\Users plus N folders; FSA_HOOK_AT_SIZED for the size pass), and the folder count at cancel is recorded (foldersAtCancel). Checked on a small root (X-003, -Prepare -Smoke): closing the window mid-scan exits 70 and writes NO report, so for closed runs the hook log is the record.
m7: -Report prints UNDECIDED, never PASS, when a needed mark or field is null. Pinned by PoolWatchReportTests mark-missing and tags-null.

N1: arm P reads ScanArm L's --list-out halves (FNV-1a 64 of the upper-cased path; even goes to A, odd to B), so it cannot reach the store. Added this attempt: after L and P, -Protocol compares their WCsc rise with I0's envelope and writes an 'abort' mark, stopping before F1. -Report then gives WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED (scenario aborted-before-f1). The smoke rerun confirmed it does not misfire.

N2: an arm's WCsc rise outside the idle envelope gives WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED. ScanArm L writes a progress log every 1,000 folders. Arms are marked every 60 s. A full exe run must report skippedStores >= 1, not only opens = 0.

N3: -Prepare holds a positive control (a cold 100K-file %TEMP% tree: mark, pressure, mark, holding 60 s then 180 s). The pressure child records the minimum Available and LowMemoryResourceNotification. If no watched tag falls, the step is INEFFECTIVE and C becomes UNDECIDED. Not run here: it is part of the person's -Prepare.

N4: the design record cites 'not Shut down' to KB3211190 and #646 as sourced, not measured. The Restart half is measured: this boot's full restart took WCsc from 211,022 to 3,585. No Shut down step is required. The optional prompt is not built.

N5: the hook fires N folders after the walk passes FSA_HOOK_PAST (the store path, held by the rig outside src). -Prepare runs the trigger checks against both the fixed and the unfixed publishes. U arms are typed unfixed-*, so the new report fields are not demanded of them.

N6: -Attribute takes an optional pooltag.txt. Otherwise one findstr per folder covers drivers\*.sys and System32\*.exe, and more than one hit is recorded as 'ambiguous (N files)'. Run: WCsc/WCfc/WCri map to wcifs.sys, FMwi/FMfc/FMfn to fltMgr.sys, NtfF to ntfs.sys; File (872 files) and Toke (488) are ambiguous.

N7: the yaml patterns are case-insensitive with scoped (?i:) inside (?m), and the PoolWatch*.ps1 -Verb RunAs rule is present. Plants S14 (RunAs), S15 (fltmc on line 2) and S16 (the paste prompt, quiet) were recorded AS-RECORDED by harness.py.

X1: the report carries counts only (core.skippedStores, topLevel.notScanned; Q-016) and never writes NotScanned into unreadable. UnreadableTab counts the store apart by kind. The window case on ...\Containers (X-002) is restored and passes.

X2: -Pressure runs after the cancelled arms and before I1, with its floor at 4,608 MB, above the 4,096 MB guard. Its positive control is in -Prepare. C is routed only from post-pressure figures; an ineffective step gives UNDECIDED.

X3: every non-app walk uses robocopy /L /E /XJ (the store-size bound, the session-2 walk with /XD store). -Prepare checks that the no-link walker skips C:\Users\All Users and rejects closing-control subtrees that contain a reparse-point directory.
X4: the -Prepare reading is named Rpre. R0 is the first reading after the Restart, and the VOID rule and the 4 GiB guard key on R0. -Protocol refuses to start on a boot older than 30 min.

X5: WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED blocks A. UNDECIDED is added. Drift is per gap with bursts left out. L has a progress log and marks every minute. Pinned by PoolWatchReportTests wcsc-during-listing and idle-burst.
Y1: listing-phase cancels fire a set number of folders after the walk passes the store or C:\Users, and the count is recorded. The unfixed full and cancelled scans run after the closing control.

Y2, which also answers O-023 (m3); the 30-item cap on this array leaves O-023 no slot of its own. Rule 1 is case-insensitive and takes either separator. The "Layers" literal is forbidden outside ContainerLayerStore.cs; the walk compares full paths, so it has no name gate. The RunAs rule is present. Plants S14-S26 are 13 AS-RECORDED, and the full harness run gave 81 AS-RECORDED, exit 0.

Y3: the control is armable only if the WCsc rise is at least 50% of the entries listed and the 0x120089 rise matches it (within max(5, 0.5 x WCsc)). -Prepare prefers Windows\Globalization first. control-leaks-one gives VOID.

Y4: the store-size bound runs once in -Prepare on the current boot, with robocopy /XJ. It is stored in prepare.json next to its environment record, never run after the Restart, and never added to a total.
Y5: the anchor for the handle step is %ProgramData%, or the override's parent in tests. The store itself is never opened. The junction and subst cases run against the planted anchor.
Y6: PathOf returns empty for NotScannedRow, for a NotScanned tree node and for a NotScanned top-level row, so 'Show in Explorer' is disabled on the store everywhere.

architecture.find: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently.
architecture.replace: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently. It never opens the Windows container layer store (%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers), which it matches by path once per scan. A scan above the store records it as one folder not scanned, its size not counted and kept apart from the unreadable folders. A root at or inside the store is refused with nothing read. This holds while the precaution against wcifs.sys's leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646) is on, as it is unless the person turns it off.

deviations: The design asked for a new NotScanned EntryKind. What is built is a Folder entry flagged EntryFlags.NotScanned, plus TopLevelState.NotScanned. The store entry has to stay a Folder: folders keep firstChild/childCount in the ID slot (SetChildren), and every EntryKind switch treats non-folders as files. Core still decides it, and the App only maps the flag to words and actions.

Outside-defect workaround switch (engine standing rule; the design had none). The defect is wcifs.sys's first-touch leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646, Windows 11 25H2). Built: Core's single Workarounds list (id wcifs-container-layers, on by default); a Precautions window with one checkbox per entry that asks before turning one off; the notice beside the result and on the refusal; and 'precautions' in the report. With it off, the store is walked and a root inside it is scanned. The setting lasts for the session because the app saves nothing to disk. Both positions are exercised in Core (WithThePrecautionOffTheStoreIsWalkedAndARootInsideItIsScanned). The off position was not driven through the exe: on this PC's real store that would walk the live layer and leak until a restart.

Report shape: per the X1 decision and Q-016 the store is reported as counts (core.skippedStores, topLevel.notScanned, core.opensUnderExcludedStore), not as a {path, reason} array. The design's field name 'notScanned' appears as topLevel.notScanned and core.skippedStores.

The exclusion check sits at pop time in Run.Execute's loop, before DirectoryReader.Read, rather than inside FolderDone. FolderDone still pushes every Folder child. The check is the same single equality, and it matches the O-004/O-029 'pop-time predicate' wording.

An 8.3 root is matched by the string step, not the handle step the design described: .NET's GetFullPath, inside LongPath.NormalizeRoot, expands tilde names to their long form. Measured by ARootSpelledWithShortNamesStopsAtTheStore; the store is still left out.

Review m6 asked to confirm that closing the window mid-scan still writes --report. It does not: the app exits 70 with no report, by WindowReport's documented contract (X-003, -Prepare -Smoke). The app is unchanged, as the design requires, and the hook's 'acted ... folders=n' log line is the record for the closed runs.
FSA_HOOK_HOLD_S, named in O-040, is not built. X-003 proves the triggers on New-LargeTree (30,150 folders), which outlasts many 250 ms ticks.

PoolWatch -Prepare under -Smoke checks the triggers on -Root instead of WinSxS, so a trigger that fails to fire on a smoke run cannot become a cold walk of all of WinSxS. The real run adds a size-pass (FSA_HOOK_AT_SIZED) trigger check, because the smoke tree is sized within one tick and never shows that pass.
not_built: The person-run protocol itself, which DONE (c) needs: -Prepare on the pre-Restart boot, then Start > Restart, then -Protocol within 30 min (about 4 h), and a second session only if L is over T. A Restart is the person's action. Only the -Smoke passes ran here; they ended VOID, correctly, because the boot was older than 30 min.
fltmc filters output: it needs an administrator, and the design makes it person-pasted into fltmc.txt. The unelevated registry minifilter-instance listing is recorded instead.

-Prepare's pressure positive control (a cold 100K-file tree) and its real WinSxS trigger checks were not run here. Both cost hundreds of MB of pool. Build attempt 1 was stopped by the engine at +0.54 GB, plausibly by those WinSxS checks.
The optional Shut down leg in -Prepare (N4): the decision allows it but does not require it.
Brief step 3's switch-off-one-behaviour narrowing of SC-070/074 and SC-067. The design left those unchanged; the protocol's S/P split and cancelled runs cover SC-011 and SC-017.
